text: SQLite and DuckDB both position themselves as in-process, local data engines rather than client/server databases.
scope: as stated by each project's own documentation, as of 2026-10-24
reason: Two official sources from independent projects use matching positioning.

text: SQLite's own documentation frames it as a local storage and application file format, explicitly not competing with server databases.
reason: Two pages of the same official documentation agree.

text: DuckDB targets analytical workloads, ships with no external dependencies, and embeds in the host process.
reason: Official project page states all three properties directly.

text: The exact boundary where analytical workloads should move from SQLite to DuckDB can be decided from official documentation alone.
reason: Both projects' docs describe overlapping niches (SQLite: works fine below 100K hits/day; DuckDB: built for analytical use cases) but neither provides comparative benchmark evidence; deciding requires workload-specific benchmarks, recorded here as insufficient instead of guessing.
